papers.title: A pseudo-labeling approach for automated assignment of unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues.
papers.abstract: In the era of AI-driven protein structure prediction, there is an urgent demand for rapid, accessible experimental approaches to validate computationally predicted structural models or to improve the accuracy of AI-based structure determination. As a key experimental technique for determining protein structures in solution, conventional biomolecular NMR spectroscopy relies heavily on proteins labeled with 13C and 15N isotopes, a requirement that entails high experimental costs, lengthy sample preparation times, and steep technical barriers, thereby limiting its broader application. Building on
papers.summary: This paper presents a pseudo-labeling method that enables automated NMR assignment of proteins larger than 100 amino acid residues without requiring full 13C/15N isotopic labeling. The approach lowers the cost and technical barrier of NMR-based structural validation, making it more practical to experimentally check AI-predicted protein models.

papers.title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells.
papers.abstract: The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and direct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used structure-guided rational design and directed evolution to create an orthogonal HaloTag variant that can be used alongside the original HaloTag for multiplexed labeling in cells. This enables simultaneous installation of different functional small molecules with high spatial and temporal control, overcoming the previous single-channel limitation of self-labeling protein tools.

papers.title: Syndirella: synthesis-directed fragment elaboration enables extensive and cost-effective binding site exploration beyond catalog compounds.
papers.abstract: Fragment screens provide an information-rich starting point for designing derivative compounds in structure-based drug discovery. However, derivatives in the fragment-to-hit stage are typically designed from only one or a few fragments, risking premature convergence on an unproductive series and dramatically limiting exploration of the binding site's interaction opportunities. This is avoidable by exploring a broad, chemically diverse set of scaffolds and elaborations spanning interactions revealed across many fragments, as well as those not yet observed. Conventional catalog procurement makes
papers.summary: Syndirella is a computational workflow that designs derivative compounds from many fragment screening hits rather than just one or a few, enabling broader exploration of a binding site's interaction opportunities. By directing synthesis toward diverse scaffolds and elaborations, it helps avoid premature convergence on unproductive chemical series and makes fragment-to-hit elaboration more cost-effective than relying on catalog compounds alone.

papers.title: Single-Particle STORM Imaging Quantifies Coating Heterogeneity Among Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) are a potentially transformative biomimetic targeted-delivery platform, which can engage therapeutic targets through source-cell membrane protein functions or homotypic interactions. However, their therapeutic development is limited by the current inability to accurately resolve membrane coating completeness, and CNP particle-to-particle variation. Here, we introduce a STochastic Optical Reconstruction Microscopy (STORM)-based approach that resolves population composition and quantifies membrane coating coverage at the single-particle level. Applying i
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a STORM super-resolution imaging method to measure how completely individual cell membrane-coated nanoparticles are covered by their membrane coating, revealing substantial particle-to-particle heterogeneity that bulk assays miss. The approach resolves population composition at the single-particle level, addressing a key bottleneck in the therapeutic development of these biomimetic delivery platforms.

papers.title: Fixed Nonsynonymous vOka Vaccine Mutations in IE62 drive Varicella-Zoster Virus Attenuation in Human Skin.
papers.abstract: The live, attenuated vaccine for Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV) protects against chickenpox in children and adults. However, the vaccine strain Oka (vOka) establishes latency and may reactivate. The molecular basis of vOka attenuation remains unknown. We investigated whether three high-frequency single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that differentiate vOka from parental strain Oka (pOka) are responsible: S628G and R958G in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62, and *130R in the membrane protein ORF0. We evaluated how these fixed SNPs mediate the attenuated growth phenotype of VZV and dimi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies three fixed nonsynonymous mutations that distinguish the attenuated varicella-zoster vaccine strain (vOka) from its parental strain, focusing on two mutations in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62 (S628G, R958G) and one in the membrane protein ORF0. Using human skin tissue models, the authors show that the IE62 mutations are the primary drivers of the vaccine's attenuated growth phenotype. This provides a molecular explanation for how the live vaccine is weakened while retaining its ability to establish latency.

papers.title: Research Progress on Irradiation Damage in High-Performance Nickel-Based Alloys for Advanced Reactors.
papers.abstract: Gen-IV nuclear systems demand structural materials with superior high-temperature mechanical integrity, corrosion resistance, and irradiation tolerance. Nickel-based alloys, owing to their excellent high-temperature properties, chemical stability, and irradiation resistance, have become leading candidate materials for key components in advanced reactors such as molten salt reactors and very-high-temperature gas-cooled reactors. This review comprehensively surveys typical reactor-grade nickel-based alloys-Hastelloy N/GH3535, Inconel 718, and Inconel 617-covering their in-service behavior, key p
papers.summary: This review surveys irradiation damage in three reactor-grade nickel-based alloys (Hastelloy N/GH3535, Inconel 718, and Inconel 617) that are candidate structural materials for Gen-IV reactors such as molten salt and very-high-temperature gas-cooled reactors. It covers their in-service behavior and key performance characteristics under irradiation, consolidating current understanding of how these alloys degrade in advanced reactor environments.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This case study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the transcription factor GABPA in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any known diagnostic category. The tumors show capillary-venous features distinct from infantile hemangioma and a prominent perivascular cell layer, suggesting GABPA dysfunction may drive a previously unrecognized vascular disorder.

papers.title: Zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorods as the therapeutic adjuvants for photothermal enhanced chemodynamic therapy and metalloimmunotherapy against tumor.
papers.abstract: Traditional tumor therapies have limited efficacy, leading to a high mortality rate. Although immunotherapy holds considerable therapeutic promise, clinical immunotherapy for solid tumors only elicits durable responses in a minority of patients. This limitation is largely attributed to the highly immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Notably, conventional chemodynamic therapy (CDT) is hampered by endogenous hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) shortage in tumor cells, and AZP compensates this defect via in-situ H2O2 self-supplementation to amplify hydroxyl radical generation.
papers.summary: This study develops zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorods (AZP) as a multifunctional therapeutic adjuvant that combines photothermal therapy, chemodynamic therapy, and metalloimmunotherapy against tumors. The zinc peroxide coating self-supplies hydrogen peroxide in situ, overcoming the typical shortage of this substrate that limits conventional chemodynamic therapy, thereby amplifying hydroxyl radical generation. The approach also leverages zinc ions to modulate the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and enhance anti-tumor immune responses.

papers.title: Capturing Hu Antigen R Domain Closure Through Supervised Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Hu antigen R (HuR), an RNA-binding protein implicated in cancer, inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders, represents a challenging target for drug discovery due to its large solvent-exposed RNA-binding interface and pronounced conformational flexibility. HuR contains tandem RNA recognition motifs (RRM1 and RRM2) that undergo substantial rearrangements between an apo open state and an RNA-bound closed conformation. Here, we investigated both states using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. While the RNA-bound complex maintained a stable closed architecture, the apo form displayed extensi
papers.summary: This study used supervised molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the conformational transition of the RNA-binding protein HuR between its open apo state and closed RNA-bound state. The RNA-bound complex remained stably closed, while the apo form showed extensive flexibility, providing insight into the domain closure mechanism relevant to drug discovery targeting HuR.

papers.title: Structural insights into the ligand modulation of MRGPRX4 conformational plasticity.
papers.abstract: Chronic pruritus is a debilitating condition with limited treatment options, particularly in cholestatic liver diseases, where bile acid dysregulation is a known trigger. Although Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X4 (MRGPRX4) has recently been identified as a key mediator of bile acid-induced pruritus, the structural mechanisms underlying its inhibition remain poorly understood, hindering the development of therapeutic antagonists. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structures of MRGPRX4 in three distinct states: agonist-bound state, antagonist-bound state, and apo state. Our s
papers.summary: This study presents cryo-EM structures of the itch receptor MRGPRX4 in agonist-bound, antagonist-bound, and apo states, revealing how ligand binding reshapes the receptor's conformation. These structural snapshots clarify the mechanism by which bile acids activate MRGPRX4 to trigger chronic itch in cholestatic liver disease, and how antagonists block it. The work provides a template for structure-guided design of MRGPRX4 antagonists as anti-pruritic therapeutics.

papers.title: Molecular insights into the selective interaction of endocrine-disrupting chemicals with poly(mannuronate) in aqueous systems: a multiscale computational study.
papers.abstract: Estrogens and other steroid hormones, also known as endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), are emerging contaminants in wastewater effluent due to human activities. Although these compounds play essential roles in medical treatments and modern agriculture, their release into the environment has raised concerns because of their potential ecological and health impacts. The selective removal of EDCs from aqueous environments is a challenge due to competition with water molecules for binding sites. This work presents a systematic computational investigation of the intermolecular interactions and p
papers.summary: This computational study uses multiscale molecular modeling to investigate how endocrine-disrupting chemicals (estrogens and steroid hormones) selectively bind to poly(mannuronate), a polysaccharide component of alginate, in aqueous environments. The work characterizes the intermolecular interactions and competitive effects of water molecules at binding sites, aiming to inform the design of selective adsorbent materials for removing these emerging contaminants from wastewater. The findings provide molecular-level insight into the selectivity of EDC adsorption onto a biopolymer scaffold.

papers.title: Ultrahigh Interfacial Thermal Conductance across GaN/BAs Interfaces via Atomic-Level Engineering.
papers.abstract: The integration of gallium nitride (GaN) with ultrahigh-thermal-conductivity boron arsenide (BAs) substrates represents a promising pathway for developing next-generation high-power devices. The heat dissipation capability of such integrated systems is fundamentally governed by thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces, and buffer layers such as Al2O3 have been widely adopted to accommodate lattice mismatch and facilitate heterointegration. However, the atomic-scale structural factors governing thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces remain unclear, limiting further improvements in inter
papers.summary: This study investigates atomic-scale heat transport across interfaces between gallium nitride (GaN) and boron arsenide (BAs), a promising pairing for high-power electronics given BAs's ultrahigh thermal conductivity. The authors examine how atomic-level structural features and buffer layers like Al2O3 govern interfacial thermal conductance, aiming to identify engineering strategies that maximize heat dissipation. The work points toward atomic-level interface engineering as a route to ultrahigh thermal conductance in GaN/BAs heterostructures.

papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis.
papers.abstract: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA
papers.summary: The authors used immunoinformatics to design an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus, targeting conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein and nucleoprotein. They identified antigenic, non-allergenic T-cell and B-cell epitopes and assembled them with adjuvants, with population coverage analysis suggesting broad HLA applicability. The work is purely computational (in silico) and has not been experimentally validated.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs a pan-cancer integrative analysis of AKT1, a kinase central to the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, characterizing its expression and alterations across tumor types. It then uses structure-based drug design to screen buckwheat-derived natural compounds as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work is largely computational and preliminary, with no experimental validation reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Bo
papers.summary: This study prospectively evaluated deep-learning co-folding methods, especially AlphaFold3, on 489 newly determined Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens, using structures released after model training cutoffs to ensure independence. It provides a large-scale, unbiased benchmark of how well co-folding predicts ligand-bound structures and ranks ligands by affinity in a realistic drug-discovery setting.

papers.title: Transforming the Landscape of Drug Innovation in AI Era: AlphaFold 3 and Beyond.
papers.abstract: The traditional drug discovery and development (DDD) pipeline has long been characterized by inefficiency and high costs. The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), especially AI-based toolkits for protein structure and interaction prediction, exemplified by AlphaFold 3 (AF3), promises to reshape the landscape of drug innovation. AF3 advances structural biology by predicting protein structures and their interactions with a range of biomolecules, including nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially changing the conventional DDD paradigm, although prediction accuracy
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI tools, especially AlphaFold 3, are reshaping drug discovery by predicting protein structures and their interactions with nucleic acids, small molecules, and ions. It argues that these advances could transform the traditional drug development pipeline, while noting remaining accuracy limitations.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: PrOMet is a new deep learning method for predicting where metals bind on protein surfaces and which metal type binds there. The authors argue that the main difficulty is that candidate binding sites are spread across the whole protein surface while actual binding sites are rare, and their approach improves localization accuracy over prior methods, including on medium-resolution structures.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the structure of the antifungal protein NFAP2, which binds fungus-specific intracellular targets like glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase, to guide structure-based drug repurposing against Candida albicans. By screening existing compounds against these NFAP2-defined targets, the authors identify candidate drugs that could be repurposed as antifungals, offering a faster route to new treatments given rising resistance and limited options.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G2
papers.summary: The study presents cryo-EM structures of wild-type and G22S mutant E. coli MscL in lipid nanodiscs, revealing a closed conformation, complemented by solid-state NMR in liposomes to probe membrane-embedded dynamics. This combined approach provides atomic-level insight into the structural basis of mechanosensitive channel gating in a native-like lipid environment.

papers.title: In vivo fate-guided design of efficient delivery systems for PROTACs: From molecular rationales to clinical progress.
papers.abstract: Despite two decades of intensive molecular engineering, the clinical translation of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remains constrained by a fundamental paradox: high in vitro potency often fails to translate into in vivo efficacy due to poor pharmacokinetics (PK)/pharmacodynamics (PD) profiles and uncontrolled biodistribution. This review departs from conventional narratives centered on potency by introducing a framework focused on drug fate that explicitly connects the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion (ADME), and tumor targeting of PROTACs with the rational design of
papers.summary: This review argues that the clinical translation of PROTAC degraders is limited less by potency than by poor pharmacokinetics and uncontrolled biodistribution. It proposes a 'drug fate'-guided design framework that links ADME properties and tumor targeting to the rational engineering of delivery systems, and surveys progress toward clinical application.

papers.title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter.
papers.abstract: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavio
papers.summary: This review discusses how adding fluorine atoms to therapeutic molecules and drug-delivery nanoparticles can fine-tune their physical and biological properties, including metabolic stability, lipophilicity, acidity, and pharmacokinetics. It highlights that beyond these established effects, fluorination is emerging as a strategy to control molecular assembly and interactions with biological systems.

papers.title: Semi-Rational Design of CpNampt Mutants for Enhanced Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) Synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstract: β-Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) serves as a direct precursor of the essential cofactor NAD⁺, playing a crucial role in regulating mitochondrial function and delaying cellular aging. Synthetic biology, with its environmental and economic advantages, has become an important approach for the production of natural medicines, with the optimized design of metabolic pathways at its core. In this study, we focused on the NMN‑consuming pathway mediated by the nma1 and pof1 genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and consequently generated their double‑knockout mutant, DHSX02. Futhermore, a highly efficie
papers.summary: The authors knocked out the NMN-consuming genes nma1 and pof1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae to create a strain (DHSX02) that preserves NMN, then used semi-rational design to engineer mutants of CpNampt for improved NMN synthesis. The work demonstrates a metabolic engineering strategy combining pathway deletion with enzyme engineering to boost NMN production in yeast.

papers.title: The PTPN1/N2 Peptide Inhibitor Achieves Potent, Long-Acting Glycemic Control and Weight-Loss Dual Efficacy in Mice.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity are closely linked metabolic disorders driven by insulin and leptin resistance. Current long-acting therapies capable of addressing both conditions are dominated by incretin-based agents, which primarily achieve efficacy through appetite suppression and are frequently associated with tolerability limitations and metabolic rebound after treatment discontinuation. Alternative strategies that correct underlying signaling defects without suppressing food intake remain lacking. Protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 act as coordinated intracellular negati
papers.summary: This study describes a peptide inhibitor targeting PTPN1 and PTPN2, two phosphatases that negatively regulate insulin and leptin signaling. In mice, the inhibitor produced potent, long-lasting improvements in glycemic control and body weight loss without relying on appetite suppression, offering a potential alternative to incretin-based dual therapies. The approach addresses underlying signaling defects rather than reducing food intake.

papers.title: Rational design of a consensus bothropic metalloproteinase as an immunogen for broadly protective antivenom development.
papers.abstract: Antivenoms remain the only specific therapy for snakebite envenoming. In Bothrops venoms, Snake Venom Metalloproteinases (SVMPs) are abundant and highly diverse toxins responsible for the major local and hemotoxic effects induced by envenoming. However, currently available bothropic antivenoms fail to fully neutralize these effects, frequently resulting in permanent and disabling sequelae in affected patients. Here, we describe a rational approach to improve the SVMP neutralization potential of bothropic antivenoms using a consensus toxin. Forty SVMP sequences belonging to PI, P-II, and P-III
papers.summary: The authors designed a consensus snake venom metalloproteinase (SVMP) immunogen by aligning 40 SVMP sequences from Bothrops venoms (classes PI, P-II, P-III) to create a single antigen that captures the diversity of these toxins. The goal is to elicit antibodies with broader cross-reactivity against the highly variable SVMPs responsible for local tissue damage and bleeding in snakebite envenoming, which current antivenoms neutralize poorly. This represents a rational immunogen-design strategy to improve antivenom efficacy.

papers.title: Recovering Pressure-Independent Dilute-Gas Thermal Conductivity from Molecular Dynamics: Green-Kubo Sampling Sensitivity and NEMD Finite-Size Effects.
papers.abstract: Gas thermal conductivity is important in many engineering systems, but reliable data are not available for every gas, mixture, temperature, and pressure. Molecular dynamics can help fill this gap by predicting transport directly from molecular motion. However, gas simulations face time- and length-scale limitations that are different from those commonly encountered in liquids and solids. These limitations are not always recognized, and standard molecular dynamics tools are often used without checking whether their settings are suitable for dilute gases. This study uses the pressure-independent
papers.summary: This study examines how simulation parameters affect the accuracy of molecular dynamics predictions for thermal conductivity in dilute gases, focusing on Green-Kubo sampling sensitivity and finite-size effects in non-equilibrium MD. It shows that standard MD settings developed for liquids and solids can produce unreliable gas thermal conductivity values unless sampling and system-size effects are carefully controlled.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Experimental Validation Define RELB as an Immune-Related Prognostic Driver in Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is one of the most aggressive gynecological malignancies worldwide. The tumor microenvironment and transcriptomic alterations play important roles in OC progression and therapeutic response. Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses may facilitate the identification of prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-Omic datasets from TCGA and GEO were analyzed. Immune-related genes were first integrated with survival information and screened using a random survival forest model to identify five core genes. GO/KEGG analyses were performed on di
papers.summary: This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO to identify immune-related prognostic genes in ovarian cancer, using a random survival forest model to narrow down to five core genes. RELB was validated experimentally as a key immune-related driver of prognosis, highlighting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Optimization of enzymatic hydrolysis for generating potential multifunctional peptides from goat milk: Bioactivity evaluation, structural characterization and molecular interaction analysis.
papers.abstract: Food-derived bioactive peptides have attracted increasing interest for functional food development. In this study, goat milk proteins were enzymatically hydrolyzed to generate peptides with inhibitory activities against α-glucosidase (α-G), dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV), and xanthine oxidase (XO). Protease screening and response surface methodology were applied to optimize the composite hydrolysis process. The optimized goat milk hydrolysate exhibited inhibitory activities of 73.05 ± 1.38%, 88.63 ± 2.76%, and 80.69 ± 1.65% against α-G, DPP-IV, and XO, respectively. The active peptide fracti
papers.summary: This study optimized enzymatic hydrolysis of goat milk proteins to produce peptides that inhibit α-glucosidase, DPP-IV, and xanthine oxidase, achieving inhibition rates of 73%, 89%, and 81% respectively. The authors used protease screening and response surface methodology to tune the composite hydrolysis process, then characterized the active peptide fraction structurally and analyzed molecular interactions. The work supports developing goat milk-derived multifunctional peptides for functional foods targeting diabetes and related metabolic conditions.

papers.title: Imidazo[1,2-b]Pyrazole-1,2,4-oxadiazole Linked 1,2,3-Triazoles: Synthesis, Antibacterial, Biofilm, and In Silico Studies.
papers.abstract: The growing incidence of bacterial resistance, especially in gram-positive infections, emphasizes how urgently new antibacterial medicines must be developed. This study presents the rational design and synthesis of a series of fused imidazo[1,2-b]pyrazole-1,2,4-oxadiazole-1,2,3-triazole hybrids (8a-8n) employing a multi-step synthetic approach that includes oxidative cyclisation, amidoxime formation, Vilsmeier-mediated cyclodehydration, and Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). The synthesized compounds were assessed for their in vitro antibacterial efficacy against Bacillus subt
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of 14 hybrid molecules combining imidazo[1,2-b]pyrazole, 1,2,4-oxadiazole, and 1,2,3-triazole scaffolds using a multi-step route including CuAAC click chemistry. These compounds were tested for antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria (notably Bacillus subtilis) and for biofilm inhibition, with in silico docking/ADMET analyses supporting the results. The work is a medicinal chemistry SAR exploration of fused heterocyclic hybrids as potential anti-infective agents.

papers.title: Green Extraction of Phenolic Compounds From Pistacia lentiscus Leaves Coupled With LC-MS Characterization and Structure-Based Enzyme Inhibition Analysis.
papers.abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and urease are critical enzymes involved in various pathological conditions associated with cellular and tissue damage. Natural products are increasingly explored as safer alternatives to synthetic inhibitors. This study evaluates the phytochemical composition and enzyme inhibitory potential of Pistacia lentiscus leaves using a green extraction approach. Bioactive compounds were extracted via lactic acid-assisted ultrasound, and the crude extract was characterized for total phenolics, flavonoids, LC-MS profile, and in vitro inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and ure
papers.summary: This study uses a green lactic acid-assisted ultrasound extraction to obtain phenolic compounds from Pistacia lentiscus leaves, then characterizes them by LC-MS and tests their ability to inhibit acetylcholinesterase and urease. The work links phytochemical profiling with in vitro enzyme inhibition and structure-based analysis, supporting the leaves as a source of natural enzyme inhibitors.

papers.title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry.
papers.abstract: Protein recognition mimicry (PRM) is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies. While existing MD-based computational tools can be used to explore a particular set of mutations at a time, suitable for small-scale studies, high-throughput (HTP) exploration of protein recognition for engineering pu
papers.summary: DyME is a molecular dynamics-based computational engine that enables high-throughput exploration of protein mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry. It addresses the limitation of existing MD tools that can only handle small sets of mutations at a time, allowing large-scale screening of amino acid changes and their conformational and energetic effects. The tool is designed to support rational design of proteins with altered molecular recognition properties.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is an anticancer target, and the work demonstrates a hybrid computational pipeline for natural product drug discovery.

papers.title: Trypsinogen Pro-Region as a Molecular Scaffold for the Design of Competitive Peptide Inhibitors of Trypsin-Like Proteases.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) productivity is severely impacted by the velvetbean caterpillar Anticarsia gemmatalis Hübner, 1818 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae), a major defoliating pest in soybean-producing regions. Current management strategies rely heavily on chemical insecticides, which are associated with environmental risks and the development of resistance. Protease inhibitors have emerged as a promising alternative, as protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae is primarily mediated by trypsin-like serine proteases. In this context, the rational design of short inhibitory peptides represents
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: The authors explore using the pro-region of trypsinogen as a molecular scaffold to rationally design short competitive peptide inhibitors targeting trypsin-like serine proteases in the velvetbean caterpillar, a major soybean pest. This approach aims to provide an environmentally friendlier alternative to chemical insecticides by disrupting protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cells in the decidua (uterine lining) and peripheral blood across early and late pregnancy. It reveals dynamic changes in NK cell populations that may support maternal immune tolerance of the fetus. The findings provide a detailed molecular map of NK cell adaptation during pregnancy.

papers.title: Rational structure-guided identification of a Bcl-2-targeting peptide with antiproliferative effects on colorectal cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Bcl-2 is critical for tumour survival and serves as a promising anticancer drug target. Herein, a series of novel Bcl-2-targeted peptides were identified through structure-based virtual screening and systematic biological validation. Four candidate peptides were selected from the peptide library. MST results demonstrated that Peptide 1 exhibited the strongest apparent binding affinity towards Bcl-2 (Kd = 0.51 ± 0.03 μM), superior to VS-9 and other screened peptides. Molecular dynamics simulation, free energy landscape analysis, and MM/GBSA calculation further supported the predicted conformati
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify peptides that bind the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, then validated four candidates experimentally. Peptide 1 showed the strongest binding affinity (Kd ≈ 0.51 µM), and molecular dynamics and free energy calculations supported the predicted binding mode. The peptide also exhibited antiproliferative effects on colorectal cancer cells, suggesting a potential starting point for Bcl-2-targeting anticancer peptide development.

papers.title: A single amino acid mutation alters substrate specificity towards l-glucose in a bacterial l-galactose dehydrogenase.
papers.abstract: Structure-based mutagenesis was performed to modify the substrate specificity of bacterial l-galactose dehydrogenase from Luteolibacter sp. strain LG18, which also exhibits intrinsic l-glucose dehydrogenase activity. Based on previously reported crystal structures of the enzyme in ternary complex with l-galactose or l-glucose and NADP+, an M212Q mutant was generated and found to exhibit a pronounced preference for l-glucose. Kinetic analysis showed that the M212Q mutant displayed an approximately 20-fold higher k cat/K M value for l-glucose than for l-galactose. To elucidate the structural bas
papers.summary: Researchers used structure-based mutagenesis to alter the substrate specificity of a bacterial L-galactose dehydrogenase that also has intrinsic L-glucose dehydrogenase activity. The single mutation M212Q shifted the enzyme's preference strongly toward L-glucose, showing an approximately 20-fold higher catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM) for L-glucose over L-galactose. This demonstrates that a single amino acid change can effectively reprogram sugar substrate specificity in this enzyme family.

papers.title: Structure-based computational prioritization of Emodin-8-glucoside as a candidate ligand for the VEGFR1 kinase domain in the context of placenta previa.
papers.abstract: Placenta previa is a serious obstetric condition associated with abnormal placental implantation and hemorrhagic complications, for which no targeted pharmacological therapy is established. This study applied an integrated structure-based computational workflow to explore the intracellular VEGFR1 kinase domain as a candidate molecular target. Twenty-one phytochemicals were screened using AutoDock Vina and MOE, with Emodin-8-glucoside consistently prioritized among the highest-ranked compounds. Redocking of the co-crystallized ligand 8ST reproduced its experimental pose with a heavy-atom RMSD o
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking to screen 21 plant-derived compounds against the VEGFR1 kinase domain as a potential drug target for placenta previa. Emodin-8-glucoside ranked as the top candidate ligand across docking tools, though the work is purely computational with no experimental validation. The finding is preliminary and does not establish any therapeutic effect.

papers.title: Immunogenic cell death and tertiary lymphoid structures jointly define dysregulated antitumor immune states and therapeutic vulnerability in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are biologically distinct yet interconnected components of antitumor immunity. ICD promotes danger-associated immune activation, whereas TLSs organize local adaptive immune responses. However, how these processes jointly affect immune heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic responsiveness in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study examines how immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) jointly shape antitumor immunity in lung adenocarcinoma. By integrating these two biologically distinct but interconnected immune processes, the authors identify dysregulated immune states that link to prognosis and therapeutic vulnerability. The work suggests that combining ICD and TLS signatures could improve patient stratification and guide treatment decisions.

papers.title: Characteristics of predicated pathogenic missense variants in human genes for Mendelian disorders.
papers.abstract: Missense variants represent a major class of genetic variation and contribute substantially to the cause of Mendelian disorders. However, the genetic and protein properties governing their pathogenicity remain incompletely characterized. Existing variant pathogenicity databases, such as ClinVar, are enriched for variants in well-studied genes and therefore may not provide a representative view of pathogenic missense variants across the genome. Meanwhile, recent advances in computational pathogenicity prediction have significantly improved their predictive accuracy, enabling large-scale genome-
papers.summary: This study characterizes the genetic and protein properties that distinguish predicted pathogenic missense variants from benign ones across human genes linked to Mendelian disorders. By using computational pathogenicity predictions rather than relying on ClinVar, which is biased toward well-studied genes, the authors provide a more genome-wide view of what makes missense variants pathogenic. The work helps clarify features such as conservation, protein domain location, and amino acid changes that underlie pathogenicity.

papers.title: Hemin suppresses interferon responses in periodontal cell models through JAK2-STAT1 inhibition.
papers.abstract: Hemin, an oxidized heme species released during erythrocyte breakdown, is detectable in gingival crevicular fluid during periodontal inflammation, but its effects on local immune signaling remain unclear. We investigated whether hemin modifies cytokine-induced interferon responses in HSC-2 oral squamous cell carcinoma cells and primary human gingival fibroblasts.
papers.summary: This study shows that hemin, an oxidized heme species found in inflamed gum tissue, suppresses interferon responses in two periodontal cell models (HSC-2 oral cancer cells and primary human gingival fibroblasts) by inhibiting the JAK2-STAT1 signaling pathway. The finding suggests hemin may act as a local immunomodulator during periodontal inflammation, potentially dampening antiviral and inflammatory signaling in the gums.

papers.title: Immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant BCG expressing a multi-epitope vaccine against mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infects approximately one-quarter of the global population, of whom 5%-10% develop active tuberculosis (TB). Although Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) remains the cornerstone vaccine against severe infant TB, its efficacy in adults is limited, underscoring the need for novel TB vaccines. This study aimed to design a multi-epitope vaccine, tMEV, and validate its protective potential through bioinformatic prediction and in vivo experiments.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: The authors designed a multi-epitope vaccine (tMEV) against Mycobacterium tuberculosis using bioinformatic epitope prediction and then expressed it in recombinant BCG. In vivo experiments showed the recombinant BCG induced immune responses and provided protective efficacy, suggesting a strategy to improve on standard BCG's limited adult protection.

papers.title: Human β defensin type 2 based novel antimicrobial peptide prediction using both molecular dynamics simulation and artificial intelligence methods.
papers.abstract: The global health crisis triggered by SARS-CoV-2 has highlighted the urgent need for effective treatments. Although several anti-viral drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2 have been developed, there remains considerable interest in exploring natural antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) secreted by the human innate immune system as alternative therapeutic agents. Human β defensin type 2 (hBD-2) has been found to bind to the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 and block the virus entry. In order to design effective anti-virial drugs based on hBD-2, 32 block-mutants (mutation at more than one site simulta
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with artificial intelligence methods to predict novel antimicrobial peptides derived from human β-defensin 2 (hBD-2), which binds the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain and blocks viral entry. The authors generate and evaluate block-mutants of hBD-2 to identify variants with improved antiviral potential. The work proposes a computational pipeline for designing hBD-2-based peptide therapeutics.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the face of rising antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI can help overcome key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity that hinder translation from lab to clinic.

papers.title: Programmable synthetic engineering of adaptive microbial cell factories: from amide transforming enzymes to advanced biocatalytic systems.
papers.abstract: Microbial cell factories integrate metabolic engineering, synthetic regulation, protein engineering, and computational design to improve catalytic performance and process robustness. Within this landscape, amide transforming enzymes provide diverse functions ranging from nitrogen metabolism and hydrolysis to covalent protein remodeling. This review examines amidases, asparaginases, glutaminases, nitrilases, nitrile hydratases, acylases, and carbamylases, with particular emphasis on microbial transglutaminase (MTGase). MTGase is distinguished by its ability to catalyze covalent ε-(γ-glutamyl) l
papers.summary: This review surveys amide-transforming enzymes—amidases, asparaginases, glutaminases, nitrilases, nitrile hydratases, acylases, and carbamylases—as building blocks for engineered microbial cell factories, with special focus on microbial transglutaminase (MTGase) and its ability to covalently crosslink proteins. It frames these enzymes within a broader synthetic biology workflow combining metabolic engineering, synthetic regulation, protein engineering, and computational design to improve catalytic performance and process robustness.

papers.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
papers.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, de
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how network pharmacology is being used to understand the multi-target mechanisms by which natural products from various ethnomedicinal traditions inhibit kidney stone formation. It argues that these compounds act on multiple pathways—metabolic, crystal-induced injury, and inflammation—rather than a single target, and that network approaches can help map these mechanisms. The abstract is truncated, but the core contribution is a methodological perspective on applying network pharmacology to anti-urolithic drug discovery.

papers.title: Gastrodin alleviates mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease via candidate targeting of ACHE, S1PR5, SERPINE1, and TOP2A: an integrative computational and cellular study.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and its prodromal mild cognitive impairment (MCI) lack effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies. Gastrodin (GAS), the major bioactive compound of Gastrodia elata, exhibits pronounced neuroprotective effects. However, the precise candidate molecular targets and systematic mechanisms by which GAS protects against AD and MCI remain poorly clarified; target engagement is inferred from computational simulation rather than direct biochemical validation.
papers.summary: This study uses computational network pharmacology and molecular docking to predict that gastrodin, a compound from the medicinal plant Gastrodia elata, may act on ACHE, S1PR5, SERPINE1, and TOP2A to protect against mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease. The authors support these predictions with cellular experiments, but target engagement is inferred from simulation rather than direct biochemical validation. The work proposes candidate mechanisms for gastrodin's neuroprotective effects but does not confirm them experimentally.

papers.title: Genetic evidence and multi-omics characterization of DEHP-relevant detoxification and metabolic heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Human evidence linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited, and it remains unclear whether DEHP-relevant detoxification biology captures clinically meaningful HCC heterogeneity.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic evidence and multi-omics data to investigate whether DEHP (a common phthalate plasticizer) exposure is linked to hepatocellular carcinoma and whether DEHP-related detoxification pathways capture clinically meaningful heterogeneity in HCC. The work characterizes metabolic and detoxification heterogeneity in HCC tumors in relation to DEHP-relevant biology, though the abstract does not report specific findings.

papers.title: Placental alkaline phosphatase promotes lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and represents a potential target for statin repurposing.
papers.abstract: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disorder driven primarily by ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Emerging evidence links ectopic lipid accumulation to fibrotic remodeling and suggests a potential contribution of immune dysregulation. However, the molecular targets connecting lipid accumulation with ligamentum flavum fibrosis remain incompletely defined. We sought to evaluate the underlying mechanisms of lipid-lowering drug targets in lipid-associated ligamentum flavum fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study identifies placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) as a molecular link between ectopic lipid accumulation and fibrotic remodeling in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, a key driver of lumbar spinal stenosis. The authors propose that statins, by targeting this pathway, could be repurposed to treat the condition. The work combines mechanistic investigation with a drug-repurposing angle.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of a novel Granzyme A (GZMA) inhibitor for autism spectrum disorder through integrative transcriptomics, virtual screening, and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Granzyme A (GZMA) is a trypsin-like serine protease expressed in cytotoxic lymphocytes that cleaves gasdermin B (GSDMB) to release a pore-forming N-terminal fragment, thereby inducing pyroptosis, a lytic and pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death. This pathway has been implicated in immune dysregulation reported in a subset of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In this study, we reanalyzed the peripheral blood transcriptome dataset GSE26415 using an integrative computational framework comprising outlier-aware quality control, differential expression analysis, functional e
papers.summary: The authors reanalyzed a peripheral blood transcriptome dataset from individuals with autism spectrum disorder and identified Granzyme A (GZMA) as a potential drug target linked to immune dysregulation and pyroptosis. Using virtual screening and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations, they identified a novel small-molecule inhibitor of GZMA. The work is entirely computational and provides a candidate compound and structural rationale, but no experimental validation is reported.

papers.title: Designing a multi-epitope vaccine against La Crosse virus using immunoinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: La Crosse virus (LACV) is a mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus responsible for pediatric encephalitis, with no currently approved vaccine or targeted antiviral therapy. This study aimed to design a multi-epitope subunit vaccine targeting the conserved nucleoprotein of LACV using an integrated immunoinformatics approach. The nucleoprotein exhibited strong antigenicity and favorable physicochemical properties, including stability and hydrophilicity. Highly conserved CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes were initially predicted, from which high-affinity, non-allergenic, and non-toxic epitopes were selected.
papers.summary: This study used computational immunoinformatics methods to design a multi-epitope subunit vaccine candidate against La Crosse virus, a mosquito-borne pathogen causing pediatric encephalitis with no approved vaccine. The authors identified conserved cytotoxic T-cell, helper T-cell, and B-cell epitopes from the viral nucleoprotein and filtered them for high binding affinity, low allergenicity, and low toxicity. The work is purely in silico and has not yet been validated experimentally.

papers.title: Selective behavioral and prefrontal transcriptomic correlates of acute clozapine exposure in socially isolated mice.
papers.abstract: Clozapine is an effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but acute molecular responses to clozapine remain incompletely characterized. Social isolation rearing produces schizophrenia-relevant behavioral abnormalities and permits joint evaluation of housing and drug exposure.
papers.summary: This study examined how acute clozapine exposure affects behavior and prefrontal cortex gene expression in mice raised in social isolation, a model for schizophrenia-relevant deficits. The authors report selective behavioral changes and distinct prefrontal transcriptomic responses to clozapine that depend on housing conditions, suggesting that isolation rearing alters the molecular response to the drug.

papers.title: Metabolite profiling and molecular dynamics-based in silico evaluation of methanolic leaf extracts of Stevia rebaudiana Bertoni against α-amylase and DPP-IV.
papers.abstract: Stevia rebaudiana Bertoni is a natural sweetener with reported antidiabetic properties; however, the molecular basis underlying the interactions of its major phytochemicals with key glycaemic-regulating enzymes remains insufficiently understood. The present study employed an integrated in silico workflow to evaluate the antidiabetic potential of selected steviol-derived phytochemicals against human pancreatic α-amylase and dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV). Methanolic leaf extracts were profiled by GC-MS, and steviol, together with the principal steviol glycosides (stevioside, rebaudioside A, a
papers.summary: This study profiled the methanolic leaf extract of Stevia rebaudiana by GC-MS and used molecular docking and dynamics simulations to test steviol-derived compounds against the antidiabetic targets α-amylase and DPP-IV. The work provides in silico evidence that steviol and its glycosides can bind these enzymes, suggesting a molecular basis for Stevia's reported antidiabetic effects. Findings are computational and require experimental validation.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of graph neural networks and classical machine learning for carbapenem-resistance prediction and genomic interpretation in Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii is a hospital-associated pathogen linked to high mortality and limited treatment options. Although many resistance determinants have been identified, how they organize into coordinated systems remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study compares graph neural networks with classical machine learning methods for predicting carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii and for interpreting the genomic features driving resistance. It finds that graph-based models can capture coordinated resistance systems, offering improved predictive performance and biological interpretability over conventional approaches.

papers.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melti
papers.summary: The authors determined the crystal structure of Honey Truffle Sweetener, a fungal sweet protein with poor heat stability, and used it to guide computational mutation design. Combining Rosetta (physics-based) and ThermoMPNN (deep-learning) predictions, they built and tested a single-mutant library, yielding variants with improved melting temperatures. This demonstrates a practical workflow for engineering thermostable sweet proteins for use in processed foods.

papers.title: Underpinning hierarchical anisotropic structure formation in soy protein high-moisture extrudates by Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
papers.abstract: Plant-based meat alternatives are fibrous anisotropic food protein products that mimic the texture and palatability of animal-based foods. The main industrially scalable production technique for manufacturing such structured protein materials is high-moisture extrusion, which involves the thermo-mechanical processing, and subsequent cooling, of a hot protein melt in the presence of shear and temperature gradients. Yet, the complex mechanisms governing fibrous structure formation in plant-protein extrudates are poorly characterised, in turn limiting the rational design and optimisation of the e
papers.summary: This study uses Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) to visualize how hierarchical anisotropic structures form in soy protein high-moisture extrudates, a key process for making plant-based meat alternatives. The work provides new insight into the fibrous structure formation mechanisms during thermo-mechanical processing, which have been poorly characterized and limit rational design of extrusion processes.

papers.title: Nanozymes in Tumor Microenvironment Modulation for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central regulatory role in malignant tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, and its complexity and dynamic heterogeneity markedly limit the efficacy of current treatment strategies. Therefore, the development of novel functional materials capable of effectively remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic tolerance has become an important research direction in cancer therapy. In recent years, nanozymes, as a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity, have shown broad potential in TME intervention and
papers.summary: This review discusses nanozymes—nanomaterials that mimic enzyme catalytic activity—as tools for remodeling the tumor microenvironment to improve cancer therapy. It highlights how these materials can intervene in TME complexity and heterogeneity, potentially alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic resistance.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the glutamate transporter SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, showing its expression pattern, clinical relevance, and functional role in tumor cells. Using structure-based virtual screening, the authors identify ethyl rosmarinate as a candidate compound that targets SLC1A6, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for bladder cancer.
